question: Why did the EXP-018 off-machine hop run at 1.8-3.5 MB/s, and what does cross-site replication actually cost?

topology.workstation: macOS, in Japan for this measurement (nearest DERP Tokyo; hard NAT, no port mapping)
topology.sf_site: RTX 4090 and RTX 3090 hosts behind one easy NAT with UPnP/NAT-PMP/PCP

workstation-sf.note: heavy queueing delay; 0% loss over 30 pings

paths.relay_observation: the RTX 4090 host's path to the workstation was relayed via DERP while idle and upgraded to direct after a few pings; the RTX 3090 host was direct and just as slow, so the relay did not set the EXP-018 rate

raw_internet_uplink_mb_per_s.method: 100-256 MB POST to speed.cloudflare.com/__up; download probe against __down returned a stub and is not reported

measurements.method: scp single stream, 256 MB zero file, ssh Compression=yes (global ssh_config)
measurements.verdict: compression artifact: zeros compress to nothing

measurements.verdict: the transpacific tunnel path is the limiter tonight, not ssh

measurements.method: tar with default 10 KiB records, WSL ext4 -> /mnt/c (9p), 2.74 GB replica
tar -b 8192 (4 MiB records), same replica, same mount
checkpoint_sync.py export of the same 2.74 GB session inside the helper container
sha256 inside the helper container, single payload file

findings: The EXP-018 hop crossed the Pacific twice (workstation in Japan); the product's replication path never does. Between the two US sites a 4.5 GB replica moves in about 3.5 minutes with 8 parallel streams and about 10 minutes single-stream, not 28.

A single scp/sftp/ssh stream is bound by the SSH channel window (about 1.6 MB in flight); at 67-190 ms that is 8-14 MB/s at best. Parallel ranged reads scale it (scripts/hosts/pscp.py). More than about 8 concurrent connections trips the Windows sshd MaxStartups limit (connection resets).

The global ssh_config `Compression yes` on the workstation makes zero-filled test files meaningless and runs zlib on the sending sshd for incompressible checkpoint payloads; pscp.py forces Compression=no.
The export's 158 s was tar's 10 KiB record size against the 9p bounce (WSL ext4 -> /mnt/c); `tar -b 8192` is 8x faster on the same mount. The tool itself exports 2.74 GB in 4.9 s.

The WSL sshd alias on the NYC host is unusable (service inactive, loopback port 22 while the alias expects 2222); enabling it would let replicas skip the 9p bounce and the Windows sshd entirely. Host change; not made here.
The RTX 4090 host's tailnet path idles onto a DERP relay and upgrades to direct with traffic; the RTX 3090 host on the same NAT stayed direct. Not the rate limiter tonight.
runtime_impact: none: import and restore timings in the EXP-018 receipts are local-disk figures
